note: Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0 by reading its operation module and tests. Input format raw bytes (default, as CyberChef's Raw) or hex text; CyberChef's order of the inputs is Raw, Hex. The result is text, one 'Name: value' line per field, not CyberChef's HTML 'Text output': Source MAC first and then Destination MAC (CyberChef's order), then every VLAN tag as a block (TPID 0x8100 or 0x88a8, priority, drop-eligible bit, VLAN ID; CyberChef lists only the VLAN IDs, as one line 'VLAN: 118, 209', and masks the ID to the low 12 bits of the tag, as Forge does), the EtherType with its registry name or the length of an IEEE 802.3 frame, and the payload as hex (CyberChef: 'Data:' and hex pairs separated by spaces). Not offered: CyberChef's Return type 'Packet data' and 'Packet data (hex)' (take the payload from the last line, or use Strip ops further up the chain). A frame shorter than 14 bytes or a VLAN tag cut short is E_COERCE with the offset (CyberChef prints what it can and does not check the length).

Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0 by reading its operation module and tests. Input format hex (default) or raw bytes, as CyberChef; its Output format (Table, Data (hex), Data (raw)) is not offered. Text with CyberChef's fields in its order and wording where it is not HTML: version, IHL with the byte length, DSCP, ECN, total length, identification in hex and decimal, Flags as 0x0N with the three bits, fragment offset (Forge adds the offset in bytes), TTL, protocol (number and name), header checksum ('correct' or 'incorrect, should be 0x...', as CyberChef), addresses, options. Differences kept: the protocol shows the IANA keyword only, where CyberChef shows number, long name and keyword; the options are decoded one per line (CyberChef prints their bytes as hex); a header shorter than 20 bytes or than its IHL, a version other than 4 and an IHL below 5 are E_COERCE with the offset where CyberChef prints an 'Error:' note or undefined values.

Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0 by reading its operation module and tests. CyberChef's input and output are raw bytes and it has no arguments; Forge's format is raw bytes (default, as CyberChef) or hex text, and the output is bytes. Drops IHL times 4 bytes. Differs: Forge also drops link padding after the datagram (the payload ends at the total length when it is set and the data holds that many bytes; a total length of 0 or beyond the data keeps everything), and a version other than 4 and an IHL below 5 are E_COERCE (CyberChef checks only for 20 bytes and the IHL length).

Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0 by reading its operation module and tests. Input format hex (default) or raw bytes, as CyberChef. Text, in CyberChef's field order and names: source and destination port, sequence and acknowledgement number, data offset with the byte length, reserved bits, flags (Forge: a summary and one line per flag, NS CWR ECE URG ACK PSH RST SYN FIN), window size, checksum as stored, urgent pointer (0x hex, as CyberChef), options decoded, payload as hex. Differences kept: the window size is not scaled by the window scale option (CyberChef writes '(Scaled: n)' and scales even a SYN segment, which RFC 7323 forbids), the reserved bits are a number (CyberChef: three binary digits), the option names are the common ones with their kind (CyberChef has the IANA list and a Value object per option), a SACK option shows its blocks, and a header shorter than 20 bytes, a data offset below 5 and an option with a bad length are E_COERCE with the offset (CyberChef reads past the end or prints an 'Error:' string).

Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0 by reading its operation module and tests. Raw bytes in (default, as CyberChef's ArrayBuffer input) or hex text, bytes out. Drops data offset times 4 bytes. A header cut short or a data offset below 5 is E_COERCE (CyberChef: 'Need at least 20 bytes' and 'Input length is less than data offset', but it accepts a data offset below 5).

Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0 by reading its operation module and tests. Raw bytes (default, as CyberChef's input) or hex text; one or more records in a row. CyberChef returns JSON (an object per record with type, version as 0x hex, length, and for handshakes the parsed messages) shown as HTML tables; Forge writes text, a block per record separated by a blank line, with names (content type, TLS version, alert level and description, handshake type, about 335 cipher suites, extension names, GREASE named), and decodes ClientHello and ServerHello with server_name, supported_groups, ec_point_formats, signature_algorithms, ALPN, supported_versions, psk_key_exchange_modes, key_share, compress_certificate, record_size_limit, padding and session_ticket (others as hex). CyberChef also decodes Certificate, ServerKeyExchange, CertificateVerify, Finished, NewSessionTicket and similar messages; Forge shows only the type and length for those. Differs deliberately: CyberChef is silent on damage (a truncated header gives an empty list, a record cut short is flagged 'truncated': true); Forge raises E_COERCE with the offset for anything that is not a TLS record, a record or hello cut short, lying lengths and damaged extensions. A message that continues in the next record is shown with what the first record holds. The reading is shared as the words packets:tls-records, tls-handshakes and tls-hellos for the fingerprint ops.

Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0 by reading its operation module and tests. Input format hex (default) or raw bytes, as CyberChef. Text with CyberChef's fields and order: source and destination port, length, checksum as stored, payload as hex (CyberChef: 'Data' as 0x hex, cut at the length field). A length beyond the data is shown with the number of bytes present, 0 means up to the end; a header shorter than 8 bytes or a length of 1 to 7 is E_COERCE (CyberChef checks only the 8 bytes).

Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0 by reading its operation module and tests. Raw bytes in (default, as CyberChef's ArrayBuffer input) or hex text, bytes out. The 8-byte header is dropped; Forge also drops anything after the declared length (link padding; a length of 0 or beyond the data keeps all). A header shorter than 8 bytes or a length of 1 to 7 is E_COERCE.

Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0: its operation module was read and run on the same inputs. Bytes in, bytes out (CyberChef: text). Removes everything up to and including the first empty line. Differs: CyberChef looks for CRLF CRLF first and only then for LF LF, so a message with an LF LF before a later CRLF CRLF is cut at the second; Forge cuts at whichever comes first (CRLF CRLF, LF LF or a mix such as LF CRLF). A message with no empty line: CyberChef returns it unchanged, Forge raises E_COERCE (the header block is not closed), a deliberate choice so that a recipe notices a truncated message; a message that starts with an empty line has an empty header block, as in CyberChef. The search is on the bytes as Latin-1, so binary bodies and any encoding work.

Cross-checked in WP 5.59b against CyberChef 11.5.0: its operation module was read and run on the same inputs. Bytes in, bytes out. Decodes the chunked transfer coding of RFC 9112 section 7.1: hexadecimal chunk sizes, chunk extensions (skipped), trailer fields (skipped) and the empty line that ends the message; a bare LF is accepted for CRLF. Same output as CyberChef on well-formed bodies. Stricter: empty input, a size that is not hex or runs past the data, a missing line end after the data, a missing last chunk or trailer end and bytes after the end of the message are E_COERCE with the offset, where CyberChef stops at what it can read, silently, and works on text (characters, not bytes). Linear and bounded: the output is never longer than the input. Run Strip HTTP headers first on a whole response.
